### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via verifyMcpAccessToken (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2dc85896abda001a51b7b0991b44fb3cae925d4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ac1b855c7aedfc49c248418e25426e519747492a` — the merge of head `82a35f8cdc7f8b3c3cc61b456387ffa3074d7f99` into base `a2dc85896abda001a51b7b0991b44fb3cae925d4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ac1b855c7aedfc49c248418e25426e519747492a && git checkout ac1b855c7aedfc49c248418e25426e519747492a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a2dc85896abda001a51b7b0991b44fb3cae925d4 82a35f8cdc7f8b3c3cc61b456387ffa3074d7f99 && git checkout -B drift-repro a2dc85896abda001a51b7b0991b44fb3cae925d4 && git merge --no-ff 82a35f8cdc7f8b3c3cc61b456387ffa3074d7f99

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2dc85896abda001a51b7b0991b44fb3cae925d4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a2dc85896abda001a51b7b0991b44fb3cae925d4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK, one docs item (no code)** at head `8bebb598f6192c4e0927c952c1db9bb58a3f0d70` (Fixes #36125). Full read of `origin/main...8bebb598f6`: 6 files, all in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` plus the changeset.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 36175` at 8bebb598f6 is CLEAN (13 items):
  - Shape: draft against `main`, first line `Fixes #36125`, and no other card is bound.
  - Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Security-touching: yes`.
  - Floors: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are success.
  - Check-runs: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.
  - `mergeable_state` is clean.
- Changeset `36125-mcp-token-issue-time-ms.md` names `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (patch), and its declaration lines match the body.

**Against security#2's guard rails (7064790122, option (a)).**
- **The ms value comes only from the signed payload.** `verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims` reads `iat_ms` off the same verified payload as `iat`, and `mcpConsentAdmits` takes it as an optional last argument.
- **The claim is written by the server.** It is an `oauthProvider` claims contributor that runs at a mint only (`grantType` is a non-empty string). It has the lowest precedence in the provider's claim merge; the sources above it are server-side. Its value must also land inside `iat`'s second, so a fixed value fails closed.
- **Absent or unplaceable values fall back to the whole-second refusal, never to an admit.** `mcpTokenIssuedAtMs` requires a number that is a safe integer and whose `floor(/1000)` equals `iat`; otherwise it uses `iat * 1000`.
- **The kept rule is unchanged.** The strict `<` in `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` and the consent comparison are both untouched.
- **Pins.** Both same-second cases from the card are pinned: minted after the change is admitted, minted before is refused, each with two real tokens in one frozen second. Also pinned:
  - the no-claim fallback, with a signed-claim control leg;
  - unreadable values (string, fractional, earlier or later second, NaN, Infinity, null, object);
  - mint-only contribution.
- **Ablations A1 to A6** each turn their pin red (PR body readings).
- Refusals are asserted as `verifyMcpAccessToken(...) === null`, the file's established face for the door's `401`.

**The point the area asked me to judge: `iat_ms` is the claims callback's instant, a few ms after `iat`'s own instant.** L1 reading: acceptable as built.
- The value is the server clock at the mint, before signing, and bounded to `iat`'s second.
- If the gap crosses a second boundary, the value lands outside `iat`'s second and the whole-second rule applies, which is stricter.
- The provider gives no hook at `iat`'s own instant, so no earlier server-written value is on offer.
- The PR's Acceptance notes state the ordering.
- Whether a few-ms-later instant satisfies "issued before the change is never admitted" is a security reading, so I leave it to the contract review (security-touching). I have passed my note to the seat.

**R1 (must fix: a published page this round makes false).** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` line 371, end of the "change's moment" paragraph: "An email-change or verification link carries its issue time in whole seconds, so one minted in the same second as the change is refused as well; **so does an MCP access token.**" After this PR, an MCP token that carries the signed millisecond issue time and was minted after the change in the same second is admitted. Only a token without the claim (minted before this release), or one whose value cannot be placed, keeps the whole-second refusal.
- Fix: reword that clause so the page says what the changeset says. Leave the link sentence as it is, since it stays true.
- This is a docs-only delta. I will read only that file and the changeset if it moves.

**Not findings.**
- `Fixes` is right. The card's same-second refusal is removed for MCP tokens by option (a) as written, and the stale docblock above `mcpConsentAdmits` is corrected.
- The `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts` "Where it is wired" line is updated, and its `/verify-email` paragraph is untouched and still true.
- No `skills/**` file teaches the MCP same-second rule (`git grep` at the head).
- Clock skew between instances is unchanged, per security#2's clock note.

**Next.** A docs commit fixes R1, then I read that delta. After ACCEPT, the contract review is the seat's, through Fable.

## Contract review
Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f9e6ff6422043a16828a2d35ec10fffc955dc391`
Local-runs: probe — built the plugin-auth dependency closure and ran `mcp-token-revocation.test.ts` with three restored ablations and one deleted throwaway test, to check the new pins and judge F1; nothing left behind.
Scope: the 7 files of `0db6f8fbe0...f9e6ff6422` in full; `mcp-token-revocation.ts`, `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts` (clock and predicate, lines 165-225), `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts` (header, `endGrantRows`, `endOAuthGrants`, `endWhatTheAccountAddedBeforeAReset`), `auth-manager-after-hook.ts:286-320`; the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 `dist/introspect-DeWu79D4.mjs` (`createUserTokens`, `resolveAccessTokenClaims`, `createJwtAccessToken`, `createRefreshToken`, `handleRefreshTokenGrant`, the authorization-code grant, the introspection re-derive) and `dist/utils-BfpTo7XY.mjs` (`collectClaims`); card #36125; comments 7064790122, 7067327130, 7067857908, 7067884938; the PR body.
Security-touching: yes

### ① Derived judgments

- **Runs.** Dependency closure build (`pnpm --filter "@objectstack/plugin-auth^..." build`, exit 0); `vitest run src/mcp-token-revocation.test.ts` at the head: 27 passed (the 5 new cases among them); three ablations of my own on the new `describe`, each restored (`git status` clean): second bound deleted in `mcpTokenIssuedAtMs` ⇒ 1 failed (the unreadable-claim pin); claim ignored in `mcpConsentAdmits` ⇒ 2 failed (the AFTER pin, the no-claim control leg); `<` turned to `<=` in `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` ⇒ 0 failed in this `describe` (the equal instant is pinned at the predicate, `credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts:686-689`); one throwaway probe test for finding F1, deleted after the run.
- **The build is option (a) as written (7064790122).**
  - Written by the server only. `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:756` registers one `oauthProvider({ extensions })` access-token claims contributor; `mcp-token-revocation.ts:246-251` returns `{ iat_ms: Date.now() }` and reads nothing from the request. In the provider, `createUserTokens` fixes `iat` (mjs:1788), derives the claims (mjs:1845), then signs (mjs:1859); `createJwtAccessToken` spreads the claims first and stamps the AS-owned ones after (mjs:1367-1378).
  - No client input path reaches the value. `resolveAccessTokenClaims` (mjs:239-262) merges, lowest first: extension contributors, per-issuance `accessTokenClaims`, the plugin's `customAccessTokenClaims`, resource-row `customClaims`. Per-issuance claims come only from an extension grant's `issueTokens` (mjs:1335-1343), and no grant is registered. `customAccessTokenClaims` writes only the organization claim (`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:746-747`). Resource rows are written server-side. Nothing in the token request body, the authorization code's stored value or a DCR registration is merged into the claim set.
  - Mint only. The contributor writes only for a non-empty string `grantType` (`:250`); the introspection re-derive passes `grantType: void 0` (mjs:2358-2364).
  - Read only off the verified payload: `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts:200-203`, the same object `iat` is read from, after signature, issuer, audience and expiry verified; passed to the door at `:239`.
  - Placement and fallback: `mcp-token-revocation.ts:267-273`. The claim is used only when it is a number, a safe integer, and `Math.floor(claim / 1000) === iat`; otherwise `iat * 1000`. A string, a fraction, NaN, Infinity, null, an object, or a value in another second all take the fallback, which is the rule before this PR.
  - The kept rule: `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` is untouched (`credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts:175-179`, strict `<`), and the consent comparison (`mcp-token-revocation.ts:338-344`) is untouched.
- **Second boundary and units.**
  - Both sides are epoch milliseconds: the claim is `Date.now()`, the change time is `toMs` of the credential row's `updatedAt` (`credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts:181-185`, `:213-221`).
  - A claim equal to the change instant is admitted, as an `iat * 1000` equal to it was before.
  - A callback that runs in the second after `iat`'s fails the floor check and falls back, which is stricter.
  - A store that keeps `updatedAt` in whole seconds makes the PR a no-op: the set the PR adds is `iat * 1000 < change ≤ iat_ms`, which is empty when the change time has no sub-second part.
  - A clock stepped backwards between the two instants yields an earlier or unplaceable value, which is stricter.
- **L1-a's open point (the claim is the callback's instant, not `iat`'s).** Not a new class. Any issue time stamped after the grant is validated has the same ordering, and the provider stamps `iat` itself after validation (`handleRefreshTokenGrant` validates, then calls `createUserTokens`, mjs:2126-2200, 1786-1788). The callback adds the few milliseconds between mjs:1788 and mjs:1845 to that span, inside one second. For a password change the grant is kept by design, so the order of validation and change inside that span gives the holder nothing its refresh token does not give it a millisecond later. One timing point is with the security seat (F1).
- **Tests.** The two starred cases mint two real tokens in one frozen second around a real `/change-password` and assert the door's answer through `verifyMcpAccessToken`; the no-claim, unreadable-claim and mint-only cases pin the fallback and the contributor. My ablations confirm the second bound and the door's use of the claim are each pinned.
- **Docs and changeset.** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx:370-375` states the new rule and its fallback and leaves the link sentence true. The changeset names `@objectstack/plugin-auth` at `patch` and carries both declaration lines.

### ② Declarations

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: correct. The door admits a token it refused (minted in the second of the change, after it); no caller's accept set narrows; every JWT access token gains one claim.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: correct. Nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- Changeset level `patch`: correct for a non-protocol widening (AGENTS.md, changeset rule).
- `Security-touching: yes`: correct. The diff changes which bearer tokens the MCP door admits after a credential change.
- Docs: the published page is updated in the same PR.

### ③ Findings

- **F1 — should-fix (SECURITY).** One timing point is with the security seat. Detail is not written in this record. It is cleared either by the seat's written ruling that it is carried, with the carrier named, or by a small change in this PR that the seat agrees.
- **N1 — nit.** `iat_ms` is not in the provider's reserved claim set, and the contributor has the lowest precedence in the claim merge. Today every source above it is server-side and none writes the name. A pin that a higher-precedence source cannot move the minted value, or a line in the docblock at `mcp-token-revocation.ts:223-232` naming the precedence, would keep a later extension grant or resource claim from changing that silently.
- **N2 — nit.** A mint whose `iat` and claims callback fall on two sides of a second boundary takes the fallback, so a token minted after a change late in a second can still be refused. It fails closed and a retry succeeds; the changeset's "a value that cannot be placed" covers it. No pin mints such a token for real; the unreadable-claim case covers it with a synthetic value.
- No must-fix.

### ④ Accepted deviations

- None at this head. F1 moves here only on the security seat's written ruling.
- Clock skew between server instances is unchanged by this PR and already accepted in 7064790122.

**VERDICT: FAIL**
